_meta.note: ICD-10 codes here are illustrative/category-level references to make the schema realistic, not verified clinical coding. Before any real-world or clinical use, have a licensed medical professional verify every code, symptom mapping, severity level, and first_aid instruction against current clinical guidelines. This dataset is a structured starting scaffold, not validated medical content.

fields.id: unique slug, used as the primary key / foreign key target
fields.icd10: illustrative ICD-10 category code -- verify before real use
fields.category: infectious | cardiovascular | respiratory | neurological | endocrine | autoimmune | gastrointestinal | urological | musculoskeletal | dermatological | mental_health | emergency_trauma
fields.symptoms: list of symptom phrases used for matching (kept as plain strings for compatibility with the existing matcher)
fields.first_aid: immediate lay-person steps for moderate/emergency entries; null where not applicable (e.g. mild, chronic-only conditions)
fields.related_conditions: ids of conditions with overlapping symptoms, for differential-diagnosis cross-referencing

conditions.name: Common Cold
conditions.description: A viral infection of the upper respiratory tract, usually resolving within 7-10 days.
conditions.advice: Rest, stay hydrated, and use over-the-counter remedies for symptom relief. See a doctor if symptoms persist beyond 10 days or worsen.

conditions.name: Influenza (Flu)
conditions.description: A contagious viral respiratory illness that can range from mild to severe.
conditions.advice: Rest and fluids are key. Antiviral medications may help if started early. Seek care if breathing difficulty, chest pain, or persistent high fever occurs.
conditions.first_aid: Rest and stay hydrated. Use a fever reducer per the label if needed. Seek urgent care if breathing becomes difficult, chest pain develops, or fever is very high and doesn't respond to medication.

conditions.name: Migraine
conditions.description: A neurological condition causing intense, debilitating headaches often with other symptoms.
conditions.advice: Rest in a dark, quiet room. Consider known triggers. If migraines are frequent or severe, consult a neurologist.
conditions.first_aid: Move to a dark, quiet room and rest. Apply a cool compress to the forehead or neck. Seek urgent care if this is the 'worst headache of your life,' comes on suddenly, or is accompanied by confusion, weakness, or fever -- those can signal something more serious than a migraine.

conditions.name: Gastroenteritis (Stomach Flu)
conditions.description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, usually caused by a virus or bacteria.
conditions.advice: Stay hydrated with fluids and electrolytes. Seek medical attention if unable to keep fluids down, or if symptoms persist beyond a few days.
conditions.first_aid: Sip clear fluids or an oral rehydration solution frequently, in small amounts. Avoid solid food until vomiting settles. Seek care if there are signs of dehydration (very dark urine, dizziness, no urination for 8+ hours) or if vomiting/diarrhea contains blood.

conditions.name: Allergic Rhinitis (Allergies)
conditions.description: An allergic response to airborne substances like pollen, dust, or pet dander.
conditions.advice: Antihistamines and avoiding known allergens can help. Consult a doctor if symptoms are persistent or severe.

conditions.name: COVID-19
conditions.description: A respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, with variable severity.
conditions.advice: Test if possible, isolate, and monitor symptoms. Seek immediate care for difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain, or confusion.
conditions.first_aid: Isolate from others, rest, and stay hydrated. Monitor breathing and oxygen levels if a pulse oximeter is available. Seek emergency care immediately for trouble breathing, persistent chest pain or pressure, confusion, or bluish lips/face.

conditions.name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
conditions.description: A bacterial infection affecting any part of the urinary system.
conditions.advice: See a doctor for antibiotic treatment. Untreated UTIs can spread to the kidneys.
conditions.first_aid: Drink extra water to help flush the urinary tract. See a doctor for antibiotics -- this doesn't resolve on its own. Seek urgent care if fever, chills, or back/flank pain develop, which can indicate a kidney infection.

conditions.name: Anxiety
conditions.description: A mental health condition characterized by excessive worry and physical tension.
conditions.advice: Relaxation techniques, exercise, and talking to a mental health professional can help. Seek urgent care if experiencing a panic attack with chest pain.
conditions.first_aid: Encourage slow, deep breathing (in for 4 counts, hold for 4, out for 6). Move to a calm, quiet space. Seek urgent evaluation if chest pain, fainting, or a racing heart doesn't settle, since these can also indicate a cardiac issue and shouldn't be assumed to be anxiety without a check.

conditions.name: Depression (Major Depressive Disorder)
conditions.description: A mood disorder causing persistent feelings of sadness and loss of interest, affecting daily functioning.
conditions.advice: Talking to a mental health professional is the recommended first step -- depression is treatable. Maintaining routine, sleep, and social connection can help alongside professional care.
conditions.first_aid: Encourage the person to talk to a doctor or mental health professional; offer to help them find one or go with them. If they express thoughts of self-harm or suicide, don't leave them alone -- help them contact a crisis line or emergency services immediately.

conditions.name: Possible Heart Attack
conditions.description: A medical emergency where blood flow to the heart is blocked.
conditions.advice: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES IMMEDIATELY. Do not drive yourself. This is a life-threatening emergency.
conditions.first_aid: Call emergency services immediately. Have the person sit or lie down in a comfortable position and loosen tight clothing. If they are not allergic and it isn't otherwise contraindicated, chewing an aspirin can help -- but don't delay calling for help to look for one. Be prepared to start CPR if they become unresponsive and stop breathing normally.

conditions.name: Possible Stroke
conditions.description: A medical emergency caused by interrupted blood supply to the brain.
conditions.advice: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES IMMEDIATELY. Note the time symptoms started. This is a life-threatening emergency.
conditions.first_aid: Use the FAST check -- Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency services. Note exactly when symptoms started (critical for treatment decisions). Do not give food, drink, or medication. If unconscious but breathing, place in the recovery position on their side.

conditions.name: Possible Appendicitis
conditions.description: Inflammation of the appendix that can rupture if untreated.
conditions.advice: Seek emergency care immediately. Do not eat or drink. This requires urgent medical evaluation.
conditions.first_aid: Seek emergency care immediately. Do not eat, drink, or take pain medication/laxatives, as these can complicate diagnosis or a possible rupture. Do not apply heat to the abdomen.

conditions.name: Tension Headache
conditions.description: The most common type of headache, often linked to stress or muscle tension.
conditions.advice: Rest, hydration, and over-the-counter pain relief usually help. See a doctor if headaches become frequent or severe.

conditions.name: Asthma
conditions.description: A chronic condition causing inflammation and narrowing of the airways.
conditions.advice: Use a prescribed inhaler as directed. See a doctor to establish a long-term management plan if newly diagnosed.
conditions.first_aid: Help the person sit upright and stay calm. Use their prescribed rescue inhaler (usually 2 puffs, repeated as directed). Call emergency services if there's no improvement after using the inhaler, lips or fingertips turn blue, or they can't speak in full sentences.

conditions.name: Pneumonia
conditions.description: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid.
conditions.advice: See a doctor promptly for evaluation, which may include antibiotics if bacterial. Rest and stay hydrated.
conditions.first_aid: Seek medical evaluation promptly, especially in young children, older adults, or anyone with a weakened immune system. Seek emergency care immediately for severe difficulty breathing, bluish lips, confusion, or chest pain that worsens with breathing.

conditions.name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
conditions.description: A chronic condition where stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus.
conditions.advice: Avoid trigger foods, eat smaller meals, and avoid lying down right after eating. See a doctor if symptoms are frequent or severe.
conditions.first_aid: If chest discomfort could be cardiac rather than digestive (especially with sweating, shortness of breath, or pain radiating to the arm/jaw), treat it as a possible heart attack and call emergency services -- don't assume it's reflux.

conditions.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
conditions.description: Open sores that develop on the inner lining of the stomach or upper small intestine.
conditions.advice: See a doctor for evaluation and treatment, which may include acid-reducing medication and testing for H. pylori infection.
conditions.first_aid: Seek emergency care immediately if vomiting blood, passing black/tarry stools, or experiencing sudden severe abdominal pain -- these can indicate a bleeding or perforated ulcer.

conditions.name: Kidney Stones (Nephrolithiasis)
conditions.description: Hard deposits of minerals and salts that form inside the kidneys.
conditions.advice: See a doctor for evaluation and pain management. Most small stones pass on their own with increased fluid intake.
conditions.first_aid: Stay hydrated and use over-the-counter pain relief as directed. Seek emergency care for fever with flank pain (possible infection), inability to urinate, or pain too severe to manage.

conditions.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
conditions.description: A chronic autoimmune disorder causing inflammation of the joints.
conditions.advice: See a rheumatologist for diagnosis and disease-modifying treatment -- early treatment helps prevent joint damage.

conditions.name: Osteoarthritis
conditions.description: A degenerative joint condition caused by the breakdown of cartilage, common with age or joint overuse.
conditions.advice: Low-impact exercise, weight management, and physical therapy can help. See a doctor if pain limits daily activities or doesn't respond to basic care.

conditions.name: Type 2 Diabetes
conditions.description: A chronic condition affecting how the body processes blood sugar (glucose).
conditions.advice: See a doctor for blood sugar testing and a management plan involving diet, exercise, and possibly medication.
conditions.first_aid: For a known diabetic showing confusion, shakiness, sweating, or fainting (possible low blood sugar), give fast-acting sugar (juice, glucose tablets) if they're conscious and able to swallow. Call emergency services if they lose consciousness or don't improve within 15 minutes.

conditions.name: Hypothyroidism
conditions.description: A condition in which the thyroid gland doesn't produce enough thyroid hormone.
conditions.advice: See a doctor for blood testing. This is typically well-managed with daily thyroid hormone replacement medication.

conditions.name: Epilepsy / Seizure Disorder
conditions.description: A neurological disorder marked by recurrent, unprovoked seizures.
conditions.advice: See a neurologist for diagnosis and treatment, typically involving anti-seizure medication.
conditions.first_aid: Ease the person to the floor and clear the area of hazards. Place something soft under their head and turn them onto their side. Time the seizure. Do NOT restrain them or put anything in their mouth. Call emergency services if the seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, a second seizure follows immediately, they don't regain consciousness, or it's a first-time seizure.

conditions.name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
conditions.description: A chronic condition where blood pressure against artery walls is consistently too high; often has no symptoms until severe.
conditions.advice: See a doctor for regular blood pressure monitoring. Often managed with lifestyle changes and/or medication.
conditions.first_aid: If blood pressure is severely elevated alongside chest pain, severe headache, vision changes, or confusion, treat as a hypertensive emergency and call emergency services immediately.

conditions.name: Anaphylaxis (Severe Allergic Reaction)
conditions.description: A severe, rapid-onset allergic reaction that can be life-threatening within minutes.
conditions.advice: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES IMMEDIATELY. Use an epinephrine auto-injector if available.
conditions.first_aid: If the person has an epinephrine auto-injector, help them use it right away. Call emergency services immediately, even if symptoms improve after the injection -- a second reaction can occur. Have them lie flat with legs raised unless it makes breathing harder, in which case let them sit up. Be ready to perform CPR if they stop breathing.

conditions.name: Choking (Airway Obstruction)
conditions.description: A blockage of the airway, often by food or a foreign object, preventing normal breathing.
conditions.advice: Call emergency services immediately if the person cannot cough, speak, or breathe.
conditions.first_aid: If the person can cough or speak, encourage them to keep coughing. If they cannot breathe, speak, or cough, and you're trained, perform abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver). Call emergency services right away. If they become unresponsive, begin CPR and continue until help arrives.

conditions.name: Severe Bleeding / Hemorrhage
conditions.description: Significant blood loss from injury that can lead to shock if not controlled.
conditions.advice: Call emergency services for any heavy or uncontrolled bleeding.
conditions.first_aid: Apply firm, direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth or bandage. Don't remove a soaked cloth -- add more on top and keep pressing. Elevate the injured area above heart level if possible. Call emergency services. Watch for signs of shock (pale, cold, clammy skin; rapid pulse; confusion) and keep the person lying down and warm.

conditions.name: Burns
conditions.description: Tissue damage caused by heat, chemicals, electricity, or radiation, ranging from mild to life-threatening.
conditions.advice: Cool minor burns under running water. Seek emergency care for large, deep, or facial/genital burns.
conditions.first_aid: Cool the burn under cool (not ice-cold) running water for 10-20 minutes. Remove jewelry or tight clothing near the area before swelling starts. Do NOT apply ice, butter, or ointments. Cover loosely with a clean, non-stick dressing. Seek emergency care for burns larger than the palm of the hand, on the face/hands/genitals, or if the skin looks charred or leathery.

conditions.name: Heat Stroke
conditions.description: A dangerous rise in body temperature, often from heat exposure or exertion, that impairs the body's ability to cool itself.
conditions.advice: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES IMMEDIATELY. This is life-threatening.
conditions.first_aid: Move the person to a cool area immediately. Remove excess clothing. Cool the body with water, fanning, or cold packs to the neck, armpits, and groin. Call emergency services -- heat stroke is life-threatening. Do not give fluids if the person is not fully alert.
